'''Alexandre Dam Sarr''' ({{IPAc-en|s|ɑːr}} {{respell|SAR}}, {{IPA-fr|alɛksɑ̃dʁ saʁ}}; born 26 April 2005)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2022/player/Alexandre-Dam-Sarr|title=Alexandre Dam SARR|work=fiba.basketball|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509121723/https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2022/player/Alexandre-Dam-Sarr|archive-date=9 May 2023}}</ref> is a French professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Perth Wildcats]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). He is {{height|ft=7|in=0}} and plays as center.

==Early life and career==
Sarr was born in [[Bordeaux]], France.<ref>{{cite web|last=Akinsola|first=Luke|url=https://www.nba.com/news/beyond-the-hardwood-france-alex-sarr|title=Beyond the Hardwood: Frenchman Alex Sarr drawing international attention|work=NBA.com|date=21 November 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231229141722/https://www.nba.com/news/beyond-the-hardwood-france-alex-sarr|archive-date=29 December 2023}}</ref> He grew up in a family of basketball players, initially in Bordeaux and then later [[Toulouse]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Pantel-Jouve|first=Gabriel|url=https://www.bebasket.fr/alexandre-sarr-va-demarrer-sa-carriere-a-pert-en-australie/|title=Alexandre Sarr va démarrer sa carrière à Perth, en Australie|work=bebasket.fr|date=9 May 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509122708/https://www.bebasket.fr/alexandre-sarr-va-demarrer-sa-carriere-a-pert-en-australie/|archive-date=9 May 2023|language=fr}}</ref> He started playing basketball at the age of four.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xaIPBnMI-kM&ab_channel=PerthWildcats|title=ALEX SARR - We Got Next|work=[[YouTube]]|publisher=[[Perth Wildcats]]|date=22 September 2023|access-date=24 September 2023}}</ref>

In 2019, Sarr joined Spanish club [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]].<ref name=eurohoops>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/1224611/ex-real-madrid-prospect-alexandre-sarr-is-the-first-european-signing-of-overtime-elite-league/|title=Ex-Real Madrid prospect Alexandre Sarr is the first European οf Overtime Elite League|work=eurohoops.net|date=1 July 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509123812/https://www.eurohoops.net/en/others/1224611/ex-real-madrid-prospect-alexandre-sarr-is-the-first-european-signing-of-overtime-elite-league/|archive-date=9 May 2023}}</ref> He played two seasons for the club's cadet youth team.<ref name="eurohoops" /><ref name=wildcats>{{cite web|url=https://www.wildcats.com.au/news/french-sensation-alexandre-sarr-joins-the-perth-wildcats|title=French sensation Alexandre Sarr joins the Perth Wildcats|work=Wildcats.com|date=9 May 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509002807/https://www.wildcats.com.au/news/french-sensation-alexandre-sarr-joins-the-perth-wildcats|archive-date=9 May 2023}}</ref>

==Professional career==
In 2021, Sarr moved to the United States to join the newly established [[Overtime Elite]] league in [[Atlanta]], securing him an alternative professional pathway with a guaranteed minimum salary of at least $100,000 per year.<ref name="eurohoops" /><ref name=forbes>{{cite web|last=Zagoria|first=Adam|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/adamzagoria/2021/07/01/overtime-elite-league-signs-first-european-player-in-alexandre-sarr/?sh=4b332c8e60a7|title=Overtime Elite League Signs First European Player In Alexandre Sarr|work=forbes.com|date=1 July 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20230509124801/https://www.forbes.com/sites/adamzagoria/2021/07/01/overtime-elite-league-signs-first-european-player-in-alexandre-sarr/?sh=481e102c60a7|archive-date=9 May 2023}}</ref> He played two seasons at Overtime Elite, the first with Team Overtime<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.overtimeelite.com/team-overtime|title=Team Overtime|work=overtimeelite.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220412071353/https://www.overtimeelite.com/team-overtime|archive-date=12 April 2022|access-date=9 May 2023}}</ref> and the second with YNG Dreamerz.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://overtimeelite.com/teams/yng-dreamerz/roster|title=YNG Dreamerz|work=overtimeelite.com|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20230529123739/https://overtimeelite.com/teams/yng-dreamerz/roster|archive-date=29 May 2023}}</ref> He earned second-team All-OTE honours in 2022–23.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://overtimeelite.com/players/65c5906d-2aed-4c1c-9a11-8fc7a6ba6068|title=Alexandre Sarr|work=overtimeelite.com|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20230509125604/https://overtimeelite.com/players/65c5906d-2aed-4c1c-9a11-8fc7a6ba6068|archive-date=9 May 2023}}</ref>

==National team career==
In 2021, Sarr debuted for the [[France men's national under-17 basketball team|French junior national team]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/player/280331/Alexandre-Dam-Sarr|title=Alexandre Dam Sarr|work=fiba.basketball|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509130645/https://www.fiba.basketball/en/player/280331/Alexandre-Dam-Sarr|archive-date=9 May 2023}}</ref> and helped them win the [[2021 FIBA U16 European Challengers|FIBA U16 European Challengers]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Feldman|first=Joseph|url=https://overtimeelite.com/articles/7ef19daa-ad67-4e80-947d-8df8303c2d3d|title=Sarr Named to U17 French National Team Select|date=2 May 2022|work=overtimeelite.com|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230509130917/https://overtimeelite.com/articles/7ef19daa-ad67-4e80-947d-8df8303c2d3d|archive-date=9 May 2023}}</ref> He helped France earn bronze at the [[2022 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup|2022 FIBA U17 World Cup]]<ref name="wildcats" /> and silver at the [[2023 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2023 FIBA U19 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2023/news/spain-on-top-of-the-world-again-outlast-france-in-otthriller-for-second-title|title=Spain on top of the world again – outlast France in OT thriller for second title|work=fiba.basketball|date=2 July 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230703031833/https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2023/news/spain-on-top-of-the-world-again-outlast-france-in-otthriller-for-second-title|archive-date=3 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Woods|first=Dan|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/sarr-s-star-performance-at-world-cup|title=Sarr's Star Performance at World Cup|work=NBL.com.au|date=3 July 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230703034307/https://nbl.com.au/news/sarr-s-star-performance-at-world-cup|archive-date=3 July 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Sarr's father, Massar, is a former professional basketball player from Senegal, while his older brother, [[Olivier Sarr|Olivier]], is a player for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).<ref name="forbes" />
